opportunities.description: NSF funds scholarships for academically talented, low-income STEM students and supports evidence-based work to improve recruitment, retention, and graduation. Full proposals are due March 2, 2027, at 5 p.m. in the submitting institution’s local time.
opportunities.eligibility: Scholars must be U.S. citizens, nationals, refugees, or permanent residents; low-income by the institution's definition; have demonstrated unmet financial need; show academic ability or potential; and be enrolled at least half-time in an eligible associate, bachelor's, master's, or doctoral program in an NSF-funded discipline. Clinical degrees, Noyce-covered teacher certification, and business administration degrees (BBA, MBA, DBA) are excluded. PI must be a faculty member teaching in an eligible discipline or an academic administrator who has taught in one (Track 3 also allows education or social science researchers).
opportunities.fundingDetails: Track 1 (Institutional Capacity Building): up to $2,000,000 over up to 6 years, only for institutions with no active S-STEM or STEP award in the past 5 years; at least 50% of funds must go to scholarships. Track 2 (Implementation): up to $2,000,000 over up to 6 years; at least 60% to scholarships. Track 3 (Inter-institutional Consortia): up to $5,000,000 over up to 6 years; at least 60% to scholarships. Individual scholarships up to $15,000 per year for undergraduates and $20,000 per year for graduate students, capped at the student's unmet need. NSF expects 40 to 60 awards, about $80 to $120 million total, subject to available funds.
opportunities.geo: United States; institutions must be accredited in and have a campus located in the U.S.
opportunities.nextStep: Faculty or grants offices should review solicitation NSF 25-514, pull financial aid data on eligible low-income students in the target disciplines, line up an external evaluator, and contact an S-STEM program officer with eligibility questions well before March 2, 2027.
opportunities.notes: Funds scholarships plus evidence-based supports such as faculty mentoring, student cohorts, tutoring, internships, career services, and mental health services.
